questions.explanation: Part-to-whole relationships at a single moment are best shown with pie or stacked bar charts, though many practitioners prefer bars for readability.

questions.q: 'Accountability to Affected Populations' (AAP) primarily emphasizes accountability toward whom?
options: The people and communities a program is intended to serve
The back donor funding the program
questions.explanation: AAP centres the rights, dignity and voice of the communities affected by an intervention, not upward accountability to donors.

questions.q: Which chart type is generally the best default for showing a trend in a continuous variable over time?
questions.explanation: Line charts connect ordered time points and make trends and rates of change easy to read.

questions.q: In the 'Data Feminist' and equity-focused reporting tradition, why is disaggregated reporting important?
options: It reveals differential outcomes across groups that aggregate figures can hide
It reduces the total number of indicators
It removes the need for a baseline
questions.explanation: Aggregate averages can mask inequities; disaggregating by sex, age, disability, caste, etc. exposes who is being left behind.

questions.q: IATI, referenced in open-data commitments across the aid sector, stands for what?
options: Integrated Assessment of Targets and Indicators
questions.explanation: IATI is the International Aid Transparency Initiative, a global standard for publishing open, comparable data on development and humanitarian resources.

questions.q: A feedback and complaints mechanism is considered 'safe' primarily when it does what?
options: Protects complainants from retaliation and handles sensitive reports confidentially
Publishes all complaints publicly with names attached
Requires complainants to visit the head office in person
Only accepts complaints from staff, not community members
questions.explanation: A safe mechanism ensures confidentiality, protection from retaliation, and appropriate handling of sensitive issues such as sexual exploitation and abuse.

questions.q: When communicating uncertainty around an estimate, the most transparent practice is to report what alongside the point estimate?
options: A confidence interval or margin of error
A single decimal figure with no range
questions.explanation: Reporting a confidence interval or margin of error communicates the precision and reliability of an estimate honestly.

questions.q: 'Storytelling with data' as popularized by Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic emphasizes which core practice?
options: Focusing the audience's attention on the message using clear visual hierarchy
Adding as many data series as possible to each chart
Using 3D effects to make charts memorable
questions.explanation: The approach stresses removing clutter and directing attention to the key insight through deliberate visual hierarchy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognized weakness of pie charts for precise comparison?
options: Humans judge angles and areas less accurately than lengths
They cannot show more than two categories
They always distort the underlying totals
questions.explanation: People compare lengths (as in bars) far more accurately than the angles and areas used in pie slices.

questions.q: For a reader who is colour-blind, the most robust accessibility practice in a chart is to do what?
options: Use redundant encoding such as patterns, labels, or shapes in addition to colour
Rely only on red and green to distinguish categories
Remove all colour and use greyscale exclusively
Increase the saturation of every colour
questions.explanation: Encoding information redundantly (patterns, direct labels, shapes) ensures meaning is not lost when colour cannot be distinguished.

questions.q: A results report that presents only outputs (e.g., number of trainings held) but claims impact is problematic because it does what?
options: Conflates activity levels with actual changes in outcomes
questions.explanation: Outputs are what a program produces; claiming impact from outputs alone overstates results without evidence of outcome-level change.

questions.q: In a dashboard, the principle of 'progressive disclosure' means what?
options: Showing high-level summaries first, with detail available on demand
Hiding all data behind a password
Disclosing the budget only at year-end
Publishing raw data before it is cleaned
questions.explanation: Progressive disclosure presents overviews first and lets users drill into detail as needed, avoiding overload.

questions.q: Which is the strongest example of 'downward accountability' in reporting?
options: Sharing findings back with affected communities in accessible formats and languages
Submitting a financial audit to the donor
Filing a report with the national regulator
Presenting results to the international board
questions.explanation: Downward accountability means reporting back to the people served, in formats and languages they can understand and act on.

questions.q: The 'lie factor' of a graphic is defined as the ratio of what?
options: Size of the effect shown in the graphic to the size of the effect in the data
Number of colours to number of data points
Ink used for data to total ink
questions.explanation: Tufte's lie factor divides the visual magnitude of an effect by its actual magnitude in the data; a value far from 1 indicates distortion.

questions.q: In IATI publishing, 'traceability' refers to the ability to do what?
options: Follow funds from the original donor through intermediaries to end activities
Trace the IP address of data users
questions.explanation: Traceability links transactions across the aid delivery chain so resources can be followed from source to activity.

questions.q: A program collects complaints but never closes the loop with complainants. Which principle is being violated?
options: Responsiveness: acting on and communicating back about feedback received
questions.explanation: Closing the feedback loop (responsiveness) is essential; collecting complaints without responding undermines trust and accountability.

questions.q: Which visualization is best suited to reveal the relationship between two continuous variables across many observations?
questions.explanation: Scatter plots map two continuous variables onto x and y, exposing correlation, clusters, and outliers.

questions.q: In accessible reporting, alternative text (alt text) for a chart image should do what?
options: Convey the chart's key message and data insight, not just say 'chart'
List the hex codes of every colour used
Be left blank so screen readers skip it
questions.explanation: Good alt text communicates the substantive takeaway of the chart so non-sighted users get the same insight.

questions.q: 'Chartjunk' refers to what?
options: Non-data decoration that does not aid, and may impede, understanding
Data points that fall outside the axis range
questions.explanation: Chartjunk is Tufte's term for gratuitous visual elements that add no information and distract from the data.

questions.q: A donor requires quarterly reporting against a logframe. The MOST useful way to present indicator status is to show what?
options: Actuals against targets with variance and a brief narrative of why
A colourful photo montage of activities
questions.explanation: Comparing actuals to targets with variance and explanation lets the reader judge progress and understand deviations.

questions.q: The Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitment most directly tied to feedback mechanisms is that communities do what?
options: Have access to safe and responsive complaints mechanisms
Receive assistance based on donor preference
Provide labour in exchange for aid
questions.explanation: A CHS commitment is that affected people can raise complaints through safe, accessible and responsive mechanisms.

questions.q: When a small percentage change is reported as a large 'percentage of a percentage' (e.g., a rise from 2% to 3% called 'a 50% increase'), the honest complementary figure to also report is what?
questions.explanation: Reporting the absolute percentage-point change alongside the relative change prevents the reader from over-interpreting the magnitude.

questions.q: Which practice best supports 'graphical integrity' when comparing quantities using icons or images (pictographs)?
options: Vary the count of equally-sized icons, not the size of a single icon
Scale one icon's area to the value
Scale one icon's height to the value while keeping width fixed
Use 3D icons that grow in volume
questions.explanation: Resizing a single icon distorts area perception; repeating identical unit icons preserves an honest comparison.

questions.q: A results framework's 'assumptions' column is important in reporting because it does what?
options: Documents external conditions that must hold for the results logic to work
Records the colour scheme of dashboards
questions.explanation: Assumptions capture external factors outside the program's control that condition whether results will be achieved.

questions.q: In dashboard design, a 'KPI card' or 'big number' tile is best used to do what?
options: Highlight a single headline metric prominently at a glance
questions.explanation: Big-number tiles surface one key metric for immediate reading; detail belongs in supporting charts.

questions.q: Publishing program data as 'open data' typically requires that it be released under what condition?
options: A licence permitting reuse, in a machine-readable format
A password shared only with the donor
A scanned PDF with a watermark
An NDA signed by each user
questions.explanation: Open data must be openly licensed for reuse and provided in machine-readable formats, not locked in inaccessible files.

questions.q: Which of the following is the clearest example of 'cherry-picking' in a results report?
options: Reporting only the districts where targets were met and omitting the rest
questions.explanation: Selectively reporting only favourable results while suppressing unfavourable ones is cherry-picking and misleads readers.

questions.q: For time-series data with strong seasonality, a useful Tufte technique to compare many periods compactly is what?
options: Small multiples (a series of small, identical charts)
questions.explanation: Small multiples repeat the same chart design across categories or periods, enabling rapid visual comparison.

questions.q: An accountability best practice when a program cannot meet a community's expressed need is to do what?
options: Communicate transparently about what can and cannot be done, and why
Ignore the request to avoid raising expectations
Redirect the complaint to the donor only
questions.explanation: Managing expectations through honest, transparent communication is central to accountability, even when needs cannot be met.

questions.q: Which is the most appropriate way to present a distribution of household incomes that is heavily right-skewed?
options: A histogram or box plot, and report the median alongside the mean
A pie chart of income bands
questions.explanation: Skewed distributions are better summarized with the median and shown as histograms/box plots, since the mean can mislead.

questions.q: 'Triangulation' in reporting findings refers to what?
options: Corroborating findings using multiple data sources or methods
Dividing the sample into three groups
questions.explanation: Triangulation strengthens credibility by cross-checking findings across different data sources, methods, or perspectives.

questions.q: A common reason to prefer a horizontal bar chart over a vertical one is that horizontal bars do what?
options: Always start at a non-zero baseline
Remove the need for a scale
questions.explanation: Horizontal bars give room for long category names to be read left-to-right without rotating text.

questions.q: Which statement about reporting confidence intervals to non-technical donors is most appropriate?
options: Explain the interval in plain language, e.g., the range within which the true value likely lies
Omit intervals entirely to avoid confusion
Report only the widest possible interval
questions.explanation: Uncertainty should be communicated in plain language so decision-makers understand the reliability without technical jargon.

questions.q: In AAP, 'participation' as a quality commitment means what?
options: Affected people influence decisions that affect their lives throughout the program cycle
Staff consult the donor before decisions
questions.explanation: Genuine participation gives affected populations influence over decisions across the whole program cycle, not token attendance.

questions.q: A dashboard that auto-refreshes but shows a metric with a two-month data lag should do what to remain honest?
options: Clearly label the 'data as of' date and any lag
Hide the timestamp to appear current
questions.explanation: Transparent labelling of the reference date and any lag prevents users from over-trusting stale figures.

questions.q: Which is a defining feature of a 'dual-axis' chart that can mislead readers?
options: Two independent y-scales can be arranged to imply a relationship that isn't there
It cannot show time on the x-axis
It always violates the data-ink ratio
questions.explanation: Dual axes let the designer arbitrarily align two scales, potentially manufacturing an apparent correlation.

questions.q: The safest choice when reporting results for a very small subgroup (e.g., n=4) is to do what?
options: Note the small sample and avoid presenting fragile percentages as robust
Report the percentage to two decimal places
Merge it silently into a larger group
questions.explanation: Percentages from tiny samples are unstable, so the small n must be flagged and over-precise figures avoided.

questions.q: 'Machine-readable' data means data that can be what?
options: Processed automatically by software, e.g., CSV or JSON, without manual re-keying
questions.explanation: Machine-readable formats like CSV or JSON allow software to parse and reuse data without human transcription.

questions.q: In storytelling with data, the recommended treatment of a chart's non-essential gridlines is to do what?
options: Mute or remove them so they recede behind the data
Bold them in a bright colour
questions.explanation: De-emphasizing gridlines keeps attention on the data and improves the data-ink ratio.

questions.q: A key ethical practice when publishing disaggregated data on a small, identifiable minority is to do what?
options: Apply data protection and anonymization to prevent re-identification and harm
Skip consent since data is aggregated
Share raw records with all partners
questions.explanation: Disaggregation can enable re-identification of small groups, so protective measures against harm are essential.

questions.q: Which best describes a 'results narrative' in donor reporting?
options: An explanatory story that interprets the numbers, including context and challenges
A table of raw indicator values only
questions.explanation: A results narrative interprets quantitative data, providing context, explaining variance, and describing what was learned.

questions.q: When choosing colours for a sequential quantitative scale (e.g., low to high), best practice is to use what?
options: A single-hue gradient that varies in lightness
Red for low and green for high only
questions.explanation: Sequential data is best encoded by a perceptually ordered single-hue (or ordered multi-hue) gradient, not an unordered rainbow.

questions.q: The primary purpose of a 'data quality assurance' note in a report is to do what?
options: Disclose limitations in how data were collected and their reliability
questions.explanation: A data-quality note transparently flags collection limitations so readers can weigh the findings appropriately.

questions.q: Which is the most complete definition of 'transparency' in the accountability context?
options: Providing timely, accessible, and understandable information to stakeholders including communities
Publishing financial statements once a year
questions.explanation: Transparency means proactively sharing timely, accessible, and comprehensible information with all stakeholders, especially affected people.

questions.q: A report claims a program 'caused' a rise in incomes based on before/after figures with no comparison group. The main reporting flaw is what?
options: Attributing change to the program without controlling for other factors
Failing to use a pie chart
questions.explanation: Without a counterfactual or comparison group, before/after change cannot be reliably attributed to the program alone.

questions.q: In an accessible data table for screen readers, the essential structural markup is to do what?
options: Designate header cells so rows and columns are announced with context
Use colour alone to mark headers
questions.explanation: Marking header cells lets assistive technology associate data with its row and column labels for comprehension.

questions.q: Which practice most strengthens 'learning' as opposed to mere 'reporting' in a MEL cycle?
options: Reflecting on findings to adapt programming, and documenting decisions taken
Formatting the report to donor templates
questions.explanation: Learning requires using evidence to reflect, adapt, and act: closing the loop between data and decisions.

questions.q: When a headline result is uncertain due to low response rates, the most responsible dashboard treatment is to do what?
options: Display the figure with a caveat or confidence indicator rather than as definitive
Show it in the largest, boldest font with no caveat
Replace it with the target value
questions.explanation: Flagging uncertainty with caveats or indicators keeps the dashboard honest while still surfacing the available evidence.
